children: Nike is scheduled to report its fiscal first-quarter financial results after the market closes Thursday. Here is what to know.
REVENUE: The sneaker company is expected to report $11.32 billion in revenue, compared with $11.72 billion in the prior-year quarter, according to FactSet.
NET PROFIT: The Beaverton, Ore.-based company is expected to post a profit of $614.9 million, compared with a profit of $727 million the year before, according to FactSet.
ADJUSTED EARNINGS PER SHARE: Adjusted earnings are expected to come in at 44 cents a share, compared with 49 cents a share the prior year.
The stock has shed 44% this year, and recently traded at $35.54.

Investor sentiment about the sneaker industry is subdued after disappointing reports from companies such as Dick's Sporting Goods. Dick's, which recently bought Foot Locker, flagged oversupply in the broader sneaker inventory that is leading to more promotions. That has coincided with softening demand for legacy lifestyle sneakers, Dick's said.

Deutsche Bank analysts aren't optimistic about Nike's first-quarter report. They don't anticipate a sales inflection until the next fiscal year, citing the industry-wide problems, as well as Nike ceasing its online distribution with Greater China wholesale partners.

Raymond James analysts recently lowered first-quarter estimates after channel checks showed challenges were continuing for the company. Underlying demand is soft and discounting remains elevated, the analysts say. They expect Nike's gross margins will face pressure from the discounts, while its wholesale business will struggle because customers are already dealing with high inventory.
